title: 1955 AHSME Problem 36
statement: A cylindrical oil tank, lying horizontally, has an interior length of \(10\) feet and an interior diameter of \(6\) feet. If the rectangular surface of the oil has an area of \(40\) square feet, the depth of the oil is:

solutions.text:
The rectangular surface has length \(10,\) so its chord width in the circular cross-section is \(\frac{40}{10}=4.\) Half the chord is \(2,\) and the radius is \(3,\) so the distance from the center to the chord is \[ \sqrt{3^2-2^2}=\sqrt5. \] A chord of this length can lie either below or above the center. Measured from the bottom of the tank, the corresponding depths are \(3-\sqrt5\) and \(3+\sqrt5.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: The oil surface is a rectangle of length \(10\), so its width is \(4\)
In the circular end, a chord of length \(4\) lies \(\sqrt{3^2-2^2}\) from the center
